## 1.1 checking multicollinearity

```{r}
    # plot(life_2015_mod)
```

There might be multicolinearity issue with some variables:

- Infant_deaths

- Under_five_deaths

- Thinness_ten_nineteen_years

- Thinness_five_nine_years

Take out infant_deaths

# 3. Fitting Model - Entire Dataset
## 3.0 Pre-LME
### Most regular linear regression model
```{r lm-fitting}
lin_mod = lm(Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + 
                                   Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + 
                                   Schooling + Economy_status_Developing, 
               data = life_final)
summary(lin_mod)
```

```{r lm-model-diag}
# residual vs. fitted
plot(lin_mod$fitted.values, residuals(lin_mod), 
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted", 
     xlab = "Fitted Values", 
     ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

# qq Plot 
qqnorm(residuals(lin_mod))
qqline(residuals(lin_mod), col = "red")
```
- From the fitted vs. residual plot, seems like there's some fanning pattern - the residuals show more variance for countries (* year) with lower life expectancy. This suggest that maybe we should allow different countries to have different intercept/slope to capture those variances. 

### GEE model
```{r, eval = FALSE}
gee <- geeglm(Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + 
                                    Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + 
                                    Schooling + Economy_status_Developing, 
                     id = Country, 
                     data = life_final, 
                     corstr = "exchangeable", 
                     family = gaussian)
summary(gee)
```


## 3.1 Fit LME model
### random intercept model
```{r}
library(nlme)
lme_int <- lme(fixed = Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + 
                                   Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + 
                                   Schooling + Economy_status_Developing,
                random = ~ 1 | Country, 
                data = life_final, na.action = na.omit)
summary(lme_int)
```

### randome intercept + slope model
```{r}
lme_slope = lme(fixed = Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + 
                                   Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + 
                                   Schooling + Economy_status_Developing,
               random = ~ Year | Country, 
               data = life_final, 
               na.action = na.omit)
summary(lme_slope)
```
### Comparing 
```{r compare-the-two-lme-models}
anova(lme_int,lme_slope)
```
- Doing LRT test: it seems that the random slope didn't do that much - it is likely because the slope seems similar between different countries (they all show an upward trend). 

```{r compare-lme-inter-with-gee-and-lin-mod}
AIC(lin_mod)
# QIC(gee_model)
AIC(lme_int)
```
- The QIC for GEE model very high, and the AIC for LME model much smaller than lin mod. The best model so far is the LME model with the random intercept, it will be used to compare with MERT and MERF.

### 3.2 MERT model
```{r mert-function-definition}
MERT <- function(data, response, fixed_effects, cluster, max_iter = 100, tol = 1e-4) {
  library(nlme)
  library(rpart)
  
  data <- data.frame(data)
  data$random_effect <- 0
  prev_logLik <- -Inf
  GLL_history <- numeric(max_iter)
  
  for (iter in 1:max_iter) {
    cat("Iteration:", iter, "\n")
    
    # subtract the random effect previous estimated
    data$adjusted_response <- data[[response]] - data$random_effect
    
    # fit the tree model to the adjusted response
    tree_formula <- as.formula(paste("adjusted_response ~", paste(fixed_effects, collapse = " + ")))
    tree_model <- rpart(tree_formula, data = data, method = "anova")
    # make prediction
    data$fixed_pred <- predict(tree_model, newdata = data)
    
    # take out the fix part of the effect and leave the randome to fit LME
    data$adjusted_y <- data[[response]] - data$fixed_pred
    
    # fit LME
    lme_model <- tryCatch({
      lme(adjusted_y ~ 1,
          random = as.formula(paste("~ 1 |", cluster)),
          data = data,
          na.action = na.omit,
          control = lmeControl(opt = "optim"))
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("LME model failed to converge at iteration", iter, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    if (is.null(lme_model)) break
    
    # Update randome effect from new LME model
    re <- ranef(lme_model)
    re_vector <- re[as.character(data[[cluster]]), "(Intercept)"]
    data$random_effect <- re_vector
    
    #gll formula
    sigma2 <- lme_model$sigma^2
    tau2 <- as.numeric(VarCorr(lme_model)[1, "Variance"])
    cluster_ids <- unique(data[[cluster]])
    GLL <- 0
    for (cid in cluster_ids) {
      subset <- data[data[[cluster]] == cid, ]
      y_i <- subset[[response]]
      f_Xi <- subset$fixed_pred
      b_i <- unique(subset$random_effect) 
      Z_i <- matrix(1, nrow = length(y_i), ncol = 1)
      R_i <- sigma2 * diag(length(y_i))
      D <- matrix(tau2, 1, 1)
      
      resid <- y_i - f_Xi - Z_i %*% b_i
      term1 <- t(resid) %*% solve(R_i) %*% resid
      term2 <- t(b_i) %*% solve(D) %*% b_i
      term3 <- log(det(D))
      term4 <- log(det(R_i))
      
      GLL <- GLL + term1 + term2 + term3 + term4
    }
    GLL_history[iter] <- GLL
    cat("  GLL at iteration", iter, ":", GLL, "\n")
    
    # convergence and stopping
    if (iter > 1 && abs(GLL_history[iter] - GLL_history[iter - 1]) < tol) {
      cat("  Convergence reached at iteration", iter, "\n")
      break
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    tree_model = tree_model,
    lme_model = lme_model,
    final_data = data,
    GLL = GLL_history[1:iter]
  ))
}
```

### 3.2 MERF model
```{r merf-reconstruct}
MERF <- function(data, response, fixed_effects, cluster, max_iter = 150, tol = 1e-4, ntree = 100) {
  library(nlme)
  library(randomForest)
  
  data <- data.frame(data)
  data$random_effect <- 0
  GLL_history <- numeric(max_iter)
  
  for (iter in 1:max_iter) {
    cat("Iteration:", iter, "\n")
    
    # subtract random effects
    data$adjusted_response <- data[[response]] - data$random_effect
    
    # random forest to adjusted response
    rf_model <- randomForest(
      x = data[, fixed_effects],
      y = data$adjusted_response,
      ntree = ntree
    )
    data$fixed_pred <- predict(rf_model, newdata = data[, fixed_effects])
    
    # randome part
    data$adjusted_y <- data[[response]] - data$fixed_pred
    
    # fit on randome part
    lme_model <- tryCatch({
      lme(adjusted_y ~ 1,
          random = as.formula(paste("~ 1 |", cluster)),
          data = data,
          na.action = na.omit,
          control = lmeControl(opt = "optim"))
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("  LME model failed to converge at iteration", iter, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    })
    if (is.null(lme_model)) break
    
    # update random effect
    re <- ranef(lme_model)
    re_vector <- re[as.character(data[[cluster]]), "(Intercept)"]
    data$random_effect <- re_vector
    
    # gll
    sigma2 <- lme_model$sigma^2
    tau2 <- as.numeric(VarCorr(lme_model)[1, "Variance"])
    cluster_ids <- unique(data[[cluster]])
    GLL <- 0
    for (cid in cluster_ids) {
      subset <- data[data[[cluster]] == cid, ]
      y_i <- subset[[response]]
      f_Xi <- subset$fixed_pred
      b_i <- unique(subset$random_effect)  # scalar
      Z_i <- matrix(1, nrow = length(y_i), ncol = 1)
      R_i <- sigma2 * diag(length(y_i))
      D <- matrix(tau2, 1, 1)
      
      resid <- y_i - f_Xi - Z_i %*% b_i
      term1 <- t(resid) %*% solve(R_i) %*% resid
      term2 <- t(b_i) %*% solve(D) %*% b_i
      term3 <- log(det(D))
      term4 <- log(det(R_i))
      
      GLL <- GLL + term1 + term2 + term3 + term4
    }
    GLL_history[iter] <- GLL
    cat("  GLL at iteration", iter, ":", GLL, "\n")
    
    # check convergence
    if (iter > 1 && abs(GLL_history[iter] - GLL_history[iter - 1]) < tol) {
      cat("  Convergence reached at iteration", iter, "\n")
      break
    }
  }
  return(list(
    rf_model = rf_model,
    lme_model = lme_model,
    final_data = data,
    GLL = GLL_history[1:iter]
  ))
}
```

# 4. Error Evaluation with 10-fold CV
## 4.1 On the global dataset
```{r lin-mod-cv-function}
cv_linear_model <- function(formula, data, k = 10) {
  # create k folds
  set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
  folds <- createFolds(data[[all.vars(formula)[1]]], k = k, list = TRUE)
  
  # vector to store MSE for each fold
  mse_values <- numeric(k)
  
  # k-fold cross-validation
  for (i in 1:k) {
    # training and validation sets
    training_set <- data[-folds[[i]], ]
    validation_set <- data[folds[[i]], ]
    
    # Fit the linear model on the training set
    lm_model <- lm(formula, data = training_set)
    
    # Predict on the validation set
    predictions <- predict(lm_model, newdata = validation_set)
    
    # Compute mse
    mse <- mean((validation_set[[all.vars(formula)[1]]] - predictions)^2)
    mse_values[i] <- mse
  }
  
  # average MSE across all folds
  cv_mse <- mean(mse_values)
  return(cv_mse)
}
```

```{r linmod-cv-result}
linmod_cv <- cv_linear_model(Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + 
                                   Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + 
                                   Schooling + Economy_status_Developing, 
               data = life_final, k = 10)
linmod_cv
```

```{r function}
library(nlme)
library(caret)

cv_lme <- function(formula, cluster, data, k = 10) {
  set.seed(123)
  folds <- createFolds(data[[all.vars(formula)[1]]], k = k, list = TRUE)
  mse_values <- numeric(k)

  for (i in 1:k) {
    train_set <- data[-folds[[i]], ]
    test_set <- data[folds[[i]], ]
    
    model <- lme(formula, random = as.formula(paste("~ 1 |", cluster)), data = train_set, na.action = na.omit)
    predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_set)
    mse_values[i] <- mean((test_set[[all.vars(formula)[1]]] - predictions)^2)
  }
  return(mean(mse_values))
}
```

```{r result}

  Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI +
    Polio + Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln +
    Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + Schooling + Economy_status_Developing,
  cluster = "Country",
  data = life_final
)
lme_cv
```

```{r mert-cv-function}
cv_mert <- function(data, response, fixed_effects, cluster, k = 10) {
  set.seed(123)
  folds <- createFolds(data[[response]], k = k, list = TRUE)
  mse_values <- numeric(k)

  for (i in 1:k) {
    train <- data[-folds[[i]], ]
    test  <- data[folds[[i]], ]

    # Train MERT model on training data
    result <- MERT(train, response, fixed_effects, cluster)

    # Predict fixed effects from the trained tree on the test data
    test$fixed_pred <- predict(result$tree_model, newdata = test)

    # Predict random effects: match clusters in test to train
    test$random_effect <- 0  # default
    re <- ranef(result$lme_model)
    test_clusters <- as.character(test[[cluster]])
    re_vector <- re[test_clusters, "(Intercept)"]
    test$random_effect[!is.na(re_vector)] <- re_vector[!is.na(re_vector)]

    # Combine to get full prediction
    pred <- test$fixed_pred + test$random_effect

    # Compute MSE
    mse_values[i] <- mean((test[[response]] - pred)^2)
  }

  return(mean(mse_values))
}
```

```{r global}
    response = "Life_expectancy",

  )
))
```

```{r merf-cv-function}
cv_merf <- function(data, response, fixed_effects, cluster, k = 10, ntree = 100) {
  set.seed(123)
  folds <- createFolds(data[[response]], k = k, list = TRUE)
  mse_values <- numeric(k)

  for (i in 1:k) {
    train <- data[-folds[[i]], ]
    test <- data[folds[[i]], ]

    result <- MERF(train, response, fixed_effects, cluster, ntree = ntree)

    # Predict fixed effects from RF on test data
    test$fixed_pred <- predict(result$rf_model, newdata = test[, fixed_effects])

    # Predict random effects using test's cluster info
    re <- ranef(result$lme_model)
    test$random_effect <- re[as.character(test[[cluster]]), "(Intercept)"]
    test$random_effect[is.na(test$random_effect)] <- 0  # handle unseen clusters

    # Final prediction
    pred <- test$fixed_pred + test$random_effect

    mse_values[i] <- mean((test[[response]] - pred)^2)
  }

  return(mean(mse_values))
}
```

```{r }
    data = life_final,
    response = "Life_expectancy",
    fixed_effects = fixed_vars,
    cluster = "Country",
    ntree = 100)
  ))
```

# 5. Interpretation
## 5.1 Global Data
```{r lme}
lme_int <- lme(fixed = Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + Schooling + Economy_status_Developing, 
               random = ~ 1 | Country, 
               data = life_final, na.action = na.omit)
summary(lme_int)
```

```{r }
# Extract RF model from MERF model fit previously 
rf_merf <- merf_result$rf_model

# Compute minimal depth distribution
min_depth_merf <- min_depth_distribution(rf_merf)

# Plot
plot_min_depth_distribution(min_depth_merf, mean_sample = "all_trees") +
  ggtitle("MERF - Distribution of Minimal Depth")
```

## 5.2 SSA region
```{r }
# fit LME to SSA
lme_int_SSA <- lme(fixed = Life_expectancy ~ Year + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + Schooling, 
               random = ~ 1 | Country, 
               data = SSA, na.action = na.omit)
summary(lme_int_SSA)
```

```{r }
# fit MERF to SSA
merf_result_SSA <- MERF(
  data = SSA,
  response = "Life_expectancy",
  fixed_effects = fixed_vars_no_region,
  cluster = "Country",
  max_iter = 150,
  ntree = 100
)

# SSA
min_depth_ssa <- min_depth_distribution(merf_result_SSA$rf_model)
plot_min_depth_distribution(min_depth_ssa, mean_sample = "all_trees") +
  ggtitle("MERF - SSA: Distribution of Minimal Depth")
```

## 5.3 non-SSA region
```{r }
lme_int_non_SSA <- lme(fixed = Life_expectancy ~ Year + Region + Alcohol_consumption + Hepatitis_B + Measles + BMI + Polio + Incidents_HIV + GDP_per_capita + Population_mln + Thinness_ten_nineteen_years + Schooling + Economy_status_Developing, 
               random = ~ 1 | Country, 
               data = non_SSA, na.action = na.omit)
summary(lme_int_non_SSA)
```

```{r }
merf_result_non_SSA <- MERF(
  data = non_SSA,
  response = "Life_expectancy",
  fixed_effects = fixed_vars,
  cluster = "Country",
  max_iter = 150,
  ntree = 100
)

# non SSA
min_depth_non_ssa <- min_depth_distribution(merf_result_non_SSA$rf_model)
plot_min_depth_distribution(min_depth_non_ssa, mean_sample = "all_trees") +
  ggtitle("MERF - non-SSA: Distribution of Minimal Depth")
```


The LME for non-SSA region significantly better - closer to MERF.

```{r}
life_summary <- life_final %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_polio = mean(Polio, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_life = mean(Life_expectancy, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

ggplot(life_summary, aes(x = avg_polio, y = avg_life)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Average Life Expectancy vs. Average Polio Coverage Over Time",
       x = "Average Polio Coverage",
       y = "Average Life Expectancy") +
  theme_minimal()
```
